findings.doc_quote: ChangeType is a union of literal value, C.* condition instance, glob string, or callable (value) -> bool .
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/event_handling/predicates.py:817-826 (compare_value) - a non-callable condition goes through `coerce_to_literal_type(actual, condition) == condition`, with no glob handling. src/hassette/types/types.py:328-331 - ChangeType = FalseySentinel | V | Condition | ComparisonCondition | None, with no glob member. Ran compare_value('light.kitchen', 'light.*') and got False.
findings.explanation: A bare glob string passed as a ChangeType (to changed_to=, changed_from=, P.ValueIs, P.StateTo and the like) is compared by plain equality and is not treated as a glob. Only P.DomainMatches, P.EntityMatches, P.ServiceMatches and P.ServiceDataWhere (when auto_glob=True) auto-wrap globs. Everywhere else you need C.Glob(...) explicitly.
findings.suggested_fix: ChangeType is a union of literal value, C.* condition instance, or callable (value) -> bool. Use C.Glob(pattern) for glob matching; only P.ServiceDataWhere (with auto_glob=True) auto-wraps bare glob strings.

findings.doc_quote: condition accepts a literal value, a C.* condition instance, a glob string, or any callable (value) -> bool .
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/event_handling/predicates.py:ValueIs.__call__ calls compare_value(extracted, self.condition). compare_value (lines ~817-826) compares a non-callable with `==` after coercion, with no is_glob/Glob wrapping. Ran compare_value('light.kitchen', 'light.*') and got False.
findings.explanation: P.ValueIs does not auto-detect glob strings. P.ValueIs(source=..., condition='light.*') only matches the literal string 'light.*'.
findings.suggested_fix: condition accepts a literal value, a C.* condition instance (use C.Glob for glob matching), or any callable (value) -> bool.

summary: The page is almost entirely accurate. Predicate, condition and accessor names, signatures, defaults (auto_glob=True, DEFAULT_EXCLUDE), coercion rules, comparison operators, the ValueError on string collections, operator shorthand with chain flattening, and the accessor MISSING_VALUE behavior all match the source. The only errors are two statements (lines 123 and 142) that wrongly list a glob string as a directly accepted ChangeType or condition.
